text:
marta: Hey folks, small but nasty one: our TS types for the js-sdk are resolving differently in edge-sample vs regular node apps. Generics stop working and overloads fail at callsite after esbuild bundles.

owen: Which SDK version and which bundler config?

marta: js-sdk@1.4.8 in the example repo (edge-sample). Repro is simple:

```
import { client } from '@redwood/inference';

const r = await client<{userId: string}>({ messages: [...] });
```

TS in editor complains: "No overload matches this call" or "Generic type requires X type argument(s)" even though the call is typed. Works fine in plain node-ts project.

priya: Sounds like a declaration resolution mismatch. Are you publishing a single dist/index.d.ts with unions or separate .d.ts per entrypoint? Node's module resolution + pnpm hoisting can point TS to the wrong file.

marta: We only publish dist/index.d.ts and a single exports mapping. package.json: 

```
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"exports": { 
  ".": { "import": "dist/index.esm.js", "require": "dist/index.cjs.js" }
}
```

But in the app tsserver resolves to /node_modules/.pnpm/@redwood+inference@1.4.8/node_modules/@redwood/inference/index.d.ts which seems truncated (missing overloads).

owen: pnpm flattens differently. Also, tsconfig moduleResolution default changed in recent TS. If consumer uses moduleResolution: 'node' then TS may not consult exports/types mappings for ESM. Try moduleResolution: 'bundler'.

priya: Another factor: esbuild's "tsconfig" behavior when transpile-only is used in the app bundler chain can cause type-checking to be delegated to VScode, which uses a different resolution algorithm than the bundler. The bundled runtime may work but editor complains.

marta: Any fast workarounds for app devs? We can't require changing people's bundlers.

owen: For immediate relief: (1) consumers can add a referencePaths override in their tsconfig to point to the SDK's d.ts. e.g., 

```
"paths": { "@redwood/inference": ["node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.d.ts"] }
```

(2) Or set moduleResolution: 'bundler' in tsconfig if they use TS>=4.7.

priya: For the SDK, we should: emit dual-format declaration files (index.d.mts and index.d.cts) and add explicit "types" mappings under "exports" so TS knows which to use for import vs require. Also add smaller, single-file entrypoint d.ts that re-exports concrete typed signatures (avoid huge overload blocks).

marta: I also noticed overloads that use unknown vs any. Consumers in edge land use strict: unknown is better but some of our overloads rely on implicit any fallback which becomes unpredictable after bundling. Maybe prefer explicit generic defaults like <T = Record<string, unknown>> to help inference.\

priya: Good call. Overloads that are too greedy break inference. Replace long overload chains with a single generic signature plus narrower helper types. Keeps things simpler for compatibility.

owen: There's also a bug where declarationMap points to non-existent .ts sources in package, causing editors to try to read files that aren't published. Turn off declarationMap for the published package or ensure source maps exist.

marta: I'll open a small SDK PR: (1) add exports.types mapping for import/require, (2) emit index.d.mts / index.d.cts, (3) add a flat "index.api.d.ts" that surfaces the most-used generic signatures with defaults, (4) update README with tsconfig guidance for edge-users.

priya: Can we add an example in examples/edge-ts showing esbuild + tsconfig.moduleResolution=bundler and the minimal tsconfig entries to avoid the editor noise? That'll save a lot of support tickets.

owen: Also add a CI check that installs the package via pnpm (simulate consumer install) and runs tsc --noEmit in a minimal project to catch these resolution issues before release.

marta: Filing issue and PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/issues/489 and PR coming.

typebot: note: lint/ts job #789 failed on examples/edge-sample in CI (ts errors).

priya: Thanks — ping us in the PR for review. If anyone can share a tiny repro I'll add it to the tests.

marta: Will do, thanks! :sparkles:
